rows.source: ORR station and platform-train-interface safety
rows.verified: Platform-to-train gaps and stepping distances vary across the network and can create boarding and alighting risks.

rows.source: ORR station and platform-train-interface safety
rows.verified: Large platform gaps can present particular difficulty for disabled and older passengers and for people travelling with children or pushchairs.

rows.source: ORR station and platform-train-interface safety
rows.verified: Railway operators should reduce platform-gap risk so far as is reasonably practicable under health and safety law.

rows.source: ORR station and platform-train-interface safety
rows.verified: Improvement priorities should take account of risk, the extent of defects and the number of passengers exposed.

rows.source: ORR station and platform-train-interface safety
rows.verified: Some platform gaps cannot be eliminated fully where track curvature constrains the platform geometry.

rows.source: ORR driver-controlled operation and train dispatch
rows.verified: Train operators must maintain suitable equipment, processes and procedures for safe train dispatch.

rows.source: ORR platform-train-interface regulatory monitoring
rows.verified: Platform-train-interface risks include trap-and-drag events and falls onto the track.

rows.source: ORR platform-train-interface regulatory monitoring
rows.verified: Door-edge obstacle detection and person-on-track detection are examples of controls used to improve platform-train-interface safety.

rows.source: ORR station and platform-train-interface safety
rows.verified: Platform risk depends on geometry, curvature, rolling stock, passenger flow, accessibility needs, dispatch method and operating conditions.

rows.source: ORR station and platform-train-interface safety
rows.verified: Station and platform guidance is location-, train-, passenger-, dispatch- and time-specific and is not an exact parcel-level incident probability.

rows.source: ORR railway trespass and criminal-behaviour controls
rows.verified: Criminal behaviour accounts for most public deaths on Britain’s railways, with trespass identified as the principal cause within that category.

rows.source: ORR railway trespass and criminal-behaviour controls
rows.verified: Vandalism such as placing obstructions on the track can cause damage, injury or derailment.

rows.source: ORR railway trespass and criminal-behaviour controls
rows.verified: Rail infrastructure controllers must reduce risks to the general public so far as is reasonably practicable.

rows.source: ORR railway trespass and criminal-behaviour controls
rows.verified: Dutyholders are expected to take reasonably practicable steps to prevent unauthorised access to railway infrastructure.

rows.source: ORR railway trespass and criminal-behaviour controls
rows.verified: Trackside materials should be controlled so they cannot readily be used in acts of vandalism.

rows.source: ORR railway trespass and criminal-behaviour controls
rows.verified: British Transport Police leads on criminal damage and railway-by-law enforcement concerning trespass.

rows.source: ORR railway trespass and criminal-behaviour controls
rows.verified: Civil police may be involved where vandalism originates beyond the railway boundary.

rows.source: ORR railway trespass and criminal-behaviour controls
rows.verified: ORR monitors whether railway parties comply with legal duties to reduce risks to the travelling public.

rows.source: ORR railway trespass and criminal-behaviour controls
rows.verified: Trespass risk depends on fencing, access points, surrounding land use, human behaviour, surveillance, response and local network conditions.

rows.source: ORR railway trespass and criminal-behaviour controls
rows.verified: Railway criminal-behaviour evidence is route-, location-, access-, population- and time-specific and is not an exact parcel-level casualty probability.
